newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends sharply lower as supplies increase.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends sharply lower as supplies increase.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on confirmation Wednesday by USDA that U.S. and world supplies of wheat were increasing, traders said.

"The world has more wheat than anybody originally thought and the buyers' appetites aren't that big," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for Chicago-based FIMAT Futures USA, Inc. "Wheat (price) is going to have to become more competitive."
USDA early Wednesday tabbed 1996 U.S. wheat production at 2.296 billion bushels, above the average of analysts' expectations for 2.268 billion.

The government also increased its outlook for 1996-97 U.S. wheat carryover to 506 million bushels, nearly 100 million bushels above the August forecast for 409 million. The government also boosted its estimate for world wheat ending stocks to 117.43 million tonnes, up 8.75 million from its outlook in August for 108.68 million.
USDA further increased its outlook for Australian wheat production this year to 19.5 million tonnes, up two million from its August forecast.
Wheat closed 11 to 17-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with September down 17-1/2 at $4.44 a bushel.
"Canada will undercut us, Australia will undersell us and the EU is cranking up their subsidies," Searcy said.
Iowa Grain, LIT America, E.D. and F. Man International, Rand Financial and Refco Inc each sold one million bushels of December, traders said.
Continental Grain bought 1.5 million bushels of December and Cargill Inc bought 1.0 million December, sources said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 21,000, up from 14,726 Tuesday.

Wheat options trading featured Paine Webber selling 200 December $4.60 calls at 10 cents, Cargill Investor Services selling 200 December $4.30 puts at 9-1/4 cents and LIT America selling 200 December $4.70 calls at 8 to 8-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000, about the same as 5,031 Tuesday.
